headline: LNG supply drops 300 MMCFD, gas pressure to remain low in Titas areas
summary: Severe weather has caused a significant drop in regasified LNG supply, affecting all categories of customers under Titas Gas.
details: Severe weather has caused the supply of regasified LNG (RLNG) from terminals in Maheshkhali to drop by approximately 300 MMCFD.
Titas Gas authorities announced in a press release on Tuesday (July 7) that this reduction has led to a gas crisis.
As a result, all categories of customers within the Titas Gas service area may experience low gas pressure until the situation improves.
The Titas Gas authority has expressed sincere regret to its customers for the temporary inconvenience caused by the weather-driven supply shortage.
caption:
Gas pressure is expected to remain low across Titas Gas areas after LNG supply dropped by 300 MMCFD due to severe weather.

headline_marked: 9 killed as [[landslides hit Cox’s Bazar]] and Rohingya camps
headline: 9 killed as landslides hit Cox’s Bazar and Rohingya camps
summary: Five children among the dead after heavy rainfall triggered soil collapses in Ukhiya and Cox's Bazar city.
details: At least nine people, including five children, were killed in landslides triggered by heavy rainfall in separate areas of Cox’s Bazar. Eight of the deaths occurred in Rohingya refugee camps in Ukhiya upazila, while one person died in Cox’s Bazar municipality.

In Camp No. 11, four people were killed when soil collapsed on houses at the foothills. In Camp No. 7, a seven-year-old boy died after being buried under mud, and in Camp No. 15, a man, his wife, and their four-year-old son were killed when a hillside collapsed onto their home.
In Cox's Bazar city, 50-year-old Ali Akbar died after a portion of a hillside collapsed onto his house in the Sattar Ghona area. Two other family members were injured in the same incident.

The Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commissioner (RRRC) stated that continuous rains from Sunday morning caused the landslides. While 1,000 people have been relocated to safer centers, officials noted that some residents had ignored previous warnings to move.

The Cox’s Bazar weather office recorded over 250 millimetres of rainfall in 24 hours. Meteorologists attribute the heavy rain to a well-marked low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal combined with an active monsoon, with rains expected to continue.

UNHCR Bangladesh reports that landslides in the Rohingya camps have killed 28 people and injured 80 others between 2021 and 2026. Factors contributing to these disasters include steep terrain, high population density, and deforestation, which weakens soil stability.
